newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's car incentive scheme to be extended.
newsitem.headline: Italy's car incentive scheme to be extended.

text.p: The Italian cabinet on Wednesday approved a bill to extend the nation's car incentive buying scheme which had been scheduled to finish at the end of September, industry minister Pierluigi Bersani told a news conference.
Bersani added that the current scheme introduced by the government in January would continue but with some modifications.
Under the scheme, owners of cars over 10 years old can trade in their vehicles for scrapping and receive a price discount on the purchase of a new car.
New car sales have been increased by the scheme with new car registrations up 43.23 percent in May from a year ago.
Under the bill, in the period October 1 1997 to January 31 1998, the cash incentive for car owners to trade in their old cars for new ones will be 1.5 million lire.
Under the current cash incentive programme running from January to September, the government offered motorists a price discount of up to two million lire, a sum matched by the car manufacturers.

In the period from February 1 to July 31 1998, the incentives will be structured to be ecofriendly and give larger amounts to cars which use less fuel. For cars that consume between 7 and 9 litres per 100 km the incentive will be 1.25 million lire and for those less than 7 litres/100 km it will be 1.5 million.
Bersani said that if parliament does not approve the bill by September, then the government will make it law by decree.

Also from July 31 1998, there will be cash incentives from government and industry of four million lire for trading in an old car for a new electric-powered one and two million lire for one that runs on methane.
Bersani added that the scheme had benefitted the environment, the recovery of car production and had also helped the nation's GDP output.

The incentive scheme has had a positive effect on the Italian car market with latest figures showing June new car registrations up 50.7 percent to 222,800, and new registrations for the first half of 1997 up 31.3 percent to 1.31 million.
